upright.general: A beginner's openness can make room for an experience you cannot fully plan in advance.
upright.connection: Meet the person in front of you instead of making them fit an old relationship story.
upright.work: A small trial can teach you more than waiting for a flawless career plan.
upright.advice: Take a reversible first step and check the practical risks before committing further.

reversed.general: A fresh start loses its freedom when enthusiasm ignores consequences or fear prevents any movement.
reversed.connection: Notice the difference between enjoying spontaneity and avoiding responsibility to another person.
reversed.work: An appealing opportunity still needs a clear scope, costs and realistic expectations.
reversed.advice: Name one risk and one safeguard before deciding whether to proceed.

upright.general: Your existing skills become useful when attention, intention and action point in the same direction.
upright.connection: Let honest words be supported by behaviour rather than relying on charm alone.
upright.work: Bring the tools you already know into a focused piece of work you can finish.
upright.advice: Choose one available resource and use it toward a specific result.

reversed.general: Scattered effort or persuasive appearances can hide a gap between what is promised and what is possible.
reversed.connection: Look for consistency instead of being carried along by an impressive explanation.
reversed.work: Check whether a confident plan actually has the skills, time and resources it needs.
reversed.advice: Reduce the promises and demonstrate one thing that can genuinely be delivered.

upright.general: Quiet attention can help you recognise a feeling before you rush to explain or act on it.
upright.connection: Listen closely while remembering that intuition cannot confirm someone else's private thoughts.
upright.work: Observe the situation and gather the missing context before announcing a conclusion.
upright.advice: Write down what you sense, then separate it from what you can verify.

reversed.general: Too much outside noise, secrecy or second-guessing can make your own perspective difficult to hear.
reversed.connection: Silence may be inviting assumptions that a respectful question could clarify.
reversed.work: Unspoken information and unclear expectations deserve attention before you continue.
reversed.advice: Ask for one missing fact and give yourself space to consider the answer.

upright.general: Growth is supported by patient care, useful resources and an environment where something can develop naturally.
upright.connection: Offer warmth in ways that also leave room for each person's independence.
upright.work: A project may benefit more from thoughtful support and steady development than from pressure.
upright.advice: Nurture one promising thing without demanding immediate proof of its value.

reversed.general: Care becomes draining when you give beyond your capacity or expect growth without replenishment.
reversed.connection: Being needed is not the same as being mutually cared for.
reversed.work: An under-supported project needs realistic resources, not more personal sacrifice by default.
reversed.advice: Identify a need of your own and make room to meet it.

upright.general: Clear structure can turn good intentions into something dependable and easier to maintain.
upright.connection: Reliability and agreed boundaries can create safety without controlling the other person.
upright.work: Define responsibilities, limits and a workable plan before adding more commitments.
upright.advice: Make one expectation explicit and follow through on your part of it.

reversed.general: Structure becomes unhelpful when rigidity replaces judgement or no one takes clear responsibility.
reversed.connection: Check whether a rule protects both people or mainly preserves one person's control.
reversed.work: Unclear ownership and inflexible processes can both obstruct useful work.
reversed.advice: Keep the necessary boundary while reconsidering the rule that no longer serves it.

upright.general: Shared knowledge and established practices can provide a starting point without removing the need for personal judgement.
upright.connection: Discuss which values and expectations you genuinely share rather than assuming agreement.
upright.work: Learn the reason behind a standard before deciding how to use it.
upright.advice: Seek a trustworthy explanation and compare it with your own experience.

reversed.general: An inherited expectation may need examination before you continue to organise your life around it.
reversed.connection: Outside opinions do not have to define the form or pace of your connection.
reversed.work: A familiar method deserves review if it conflicts with the actual problem.
reversed.advice: Distinguish a meaningful principle from a habit followed only for approval.

upright.general: An important choice becomes clearer when your actions and values can agree with each other.
upright.connection: Mutual interest needs honest communication, consent and choices that respect both people.
upright.work: Consider whether an agreement fits your priorities as well as its immediate appeal.
upright.advice: State what matters most before choosing what you are willing to commit to.

reversed.general: A mismatch between priorities and behaviour can make even an attractive choice feel divided.
reversed.connection: Avoid replacing a difficult conversation with assumptions about compatibility.
reversed.work: Competing commitments may need an honest decision rather than another compromise you cannot sustain.
reversed.advice: Name the conflict and decide which value should guide the next step.

upright.general: Progress becomes more deliberate when you choose a direction and coordinate the forces pulling your attention apart.
upright.connection: A shared direction works best when neither person has to be dragged toward it.
upright.work: Set a clear target and manage distractions instead of measuring effort by speed alone.
upright.advice: Choose the next milestone and make your effort serve that direction.

reversed.general: Pushing harder may increase friction when your motives or commitments are moving in different directions.
reversed.connection: Trying to steer every outcome can leave little room for a genuine response.
reversed.work: Busy movement is not always progress; reconsider priorities before increasing the pace.
reversed.advice: Pause long enough to align the goal, the available energy and the plan.

upright.general: Steady courage can make space for a strong feeling without letting that feeling control your response.
upright.connection: Kindness and a firm boundary can belong in the same conversation.
upright.work: Patient practice and composure may accomplish more than proving your toughness.
upright.advice: Respond firmly but gently to one situation that usually draws an automatic reaction.

reversed.general: Exhaustion or self-doubt can make ordinary demands feel like tests of your worth.
reversed.connection: You do not have to tolerate hurtful behaviour to demonstrate patience or loyalty.
reversed.work: A difficult task is not evidence that you lack ability or deserve less support.
reversed.advice: Reduce the self-criticism and choose support or rest before forcing more effort.

upright.general: A period of deliberate solitude can help you identify what you think when outside expectations grow quieter.
upright.connection: Time apart can be constructive when its purpose and limits are communicated kindly.
upright.work: Focused independent study may reveal the question you need to answer next.
upright.advice: Make quiet space for reflection without cutting off useful support.

reversed.general: Reflection can turn into avoidance when you keep searching alone but no longer test your thoughts against experience.
reversed.connection: Withdrawal may leave an important need unexplained and the other person guessing.
reversed.work: Working alone on a difficulty may be less useful now than asking a precise question.
reversed.advice: Reconnect with one trusted person or a small practical task.

upright.general: Changing circumstances invite flexibility and a clearer distinction between influence and control.
upright.connection: A shift in routine can reveal how well you adapt and communicate together.
upright.work: Notice changing conditions without treating a lucky opening as a dependable plan.
upright.advice: Prepare for more than one outcome and use the options you actually have.

reversed.general: A repeating difficulty may call for an adjusted response rather than a judgement that everything is against you.
reversed.connection: Identify the pattern you repeat instead of expecting circumstances alone to change it.
reversed.work: Review contingencies when a setback exposes how much depends on one assumption.
reversed.advice: Change one part of the cycle that is within your influence.

upright.general: Fair judgement asks you to examine evidence, consequences and your own part in the situation.
upright.connection: Listen to both perspectives without using fairness to dismiss genuine differences in need.
upright.work: Review agreements and responsibilities carefully rather than relying on what seems implied.
upright.advice: Make a decision you can explain honestly and accept responsibility for.

reversed.general: Bias, missing information or avoided accountability may be making a decision less fair than it appears.
reversed.connection: A disagreement needs a clearer account of what happened, not a quick assignment of blame.
reversed.work: An uneven arrangement deserves specific questions about expectations and consequences.
reversed.advice: Check the facts and correct your part without accepting responsibility that is not yours.

upright.general: A deliberate pause can reveal a choice that constant effort has kept out of view.
upright.connection: Give each person time to see the situation without demanding an immediate answer.
upright.work: Reframe a stalled task before adding more hours to the same approach.
upright.advice: Ask what becomes visible when you stop trying to force progress.

reversed.general: Waiting stops being useful when it becomes a reason to avoid a choice or ignore your own needs.
reversed.connection: Keeping a connection at any cost can turn patience into self-erasure.
reversed.work: An indefinite delay needs a reason, a review point and permission to change direction.
reversed.advice: Decide what the pause is for and what would tell you it is time to act.

upright.general: An ending can make room for a different way of living without making the transition easy or immediate.
upright.connection: A familiar relationship pattern may need to end even if the connection continues.
upright.work: Consider which outdated commitment or method is preventing a useful next phase.
upright.advice: Name what is finished and make space for a gradual transition. This card does not predict physical death.

reversed.general: Holding on to a completed chapter may protect familiarity while prolonging the difficulty of moving forward.
reversed.connection: Notice whether hope for the old arrangement is blocking an honest conversation about the present.
reversed.work: A transition may need smaller stages, not an attempt to preserve every old condition.
reversed.advice: Release one manageable part of what no longer fits, without forcing the entire change at once.

upright.general: A workable balance can emerge from patient adjustments rather than a perfect compromise reached all at once.
upright.connection: Different needs can coexist when both people are willing to adjust their pace.
upright.work: Combine useful approaches and choose a rhythm that can be maintained.
upright.advice: Make one measured adjustment and give yourself time to observe its effect.

reversed.general: Too much intensity in one direction can make the rest of your commitments harder to sustain.
reversed.connection: A recurring mismatch in pace or effort deserves discussion rather than more silent adjustment.
reversed.work: Overextension may be disguising an unrealistic workload or a missing priority.
reversed.advice: Reduce one excess before adding another solution to the situation.

upright.general: A strong attachment deserves examination when it limits your freedom or keeps a costly pattern in place.
upright.connection: Intensity is not a substitute for respect, consent or the ability to say no.
upright.work: Question a reward or obligation that keeps asking for more than you can reasonably give.
upright.advice: Name the pattern without shaming yourself and identify a source of support.

reversed.general: Recognising a limiting attachment can open a path toward more deliberate and independent choices.
reversed.connection: A healthier connection leaves room for boundaries instead of relying on guilt or control.
reversed.work: Review which commitments you can renegotiate rather than assuming there is no alternative.
reversed.advice: Take one supported step that increases your real freedom to choose.

upright.general: A challenged assumption can reveal that a familiar structure needs attention, not that disaster is guaranteed.
upright.connection: An uncomfortable truth may call for honest conversation and a clearer sense of safety.
upright.work: When a plan proves fragile, protect what matters before rushing to rebuild it.
upright.advice: Return to the facts, stabilise the immediate situation and ask for help where needed.

reversed.general: Avoiding an uncomfortable adjustment may allow a known weakness to become more difficult to address.
reversed.connection: A difficult conversation can be approached gradually without pretending the issue has disappeared.
reversed.work: Small repairs to a weak plan may be more useful than defending how much effort it already took.
reversed.advice: Address one visible weakness while you still have room to choose the response.

upright.general: Hope can become practical when you let renewal happen through small, repeatable acts of care.
upright.connection: Openness may return gradually when trust is supported by consistent behaviour.
upright.work: A meaningful direction can restore motivation even before visible results arrive.
upright.advice: Choose a gentle action that makes the future feel more approachable today.

reversed.general: Discouragement can narrow your view of what remains possible without proving that hope was misplaced.
reversed.connection: Allowing support does not require pretending that disappointment is already resolved.
reversed.work: Compare progress with a realistic baseline rather than a distant ideal.
reversed.advice: Lower the demand for certainty and notice one sign of effort or support.

upright.general: Strong impressions and incomplete information may be sharing the same space, making certainty difficult to find.
upright.connection: Feelings deserve attention, but they cannot verify a suspicion about another person.
upright.work: Clarify unclear instructions and assumptions before treating an impression as a reliable plan.
upright.advice: Name what is unknown and check one relevant fact before drawing conclusions.

reversed.general: A confusing impression may become easier to examine when you describe it plainly and allow new information in.
reversed.connection: A careful conversation can test a fear without turning it into an accusation.
reversed.work: Write down the uncertainty so it can become a question someone can answer.
reversed.advice: Welcome useful clarification without insisting that every ambiguity must disappear immediately.

upright.general: Clarity and uncomplicated enjoyment can help you recognise what is working without needing to exaggerate it.
upright.connection: Make room for mutual enjoyment, openness and affection that can be expressed simply.
upright.work: Acknowledge a concrete success and make useful learning visible to others.
upright.advice: Enjoy one real source of satisfaction while staying honest about the remaining work.

reversed.general: Pressure to feel positive may be getting in the way of noticing quieter forms of satisfaction.
reversed.connection: You can appreciate a connection without expecting it to remove every difficult feeling.
reversed.work: Recognition may be delayed or less visible than you hoped without making the work worthless.
reversed.advice: Replace the demand for a perfect outcome with one specific thing you can appreciate.

upright.general: Honest reflection can turn experience into a deliberate choice about how you want to continue.
upright.connection: Accountability allows repair when it includes changed behaviour rather than only regret.
upright.work: Review what you learned before deciding whether to renew or redirect a commitment.
upright.advice: Acknowledge the lesson and choose one action that shows you have heard it.

reversed.general: Harsh self-judgement or an avoided review can keep an old mistake in charge of a new decision.
reversed.connection: Distinguish a request for accountability from a demand that someone remain permanently guilty.
reversed.work: Feedback becomes useful when you turn it into a specific adjustment instead of a verdict on ability.
reversed.advice: Review the evidence kindly and choose a correction rather than a punishment.

upright.general: Completion invites you to recognise what has come together and carry its lessons into the next chapter.
upright.connection: A shared milestone can be appreciated without assuming that care and communication are now finished.
upright.work: Close the loop on a piece of work and acknowledge the people and skills that made it possible.
upright.advice: Mark the achievement, finish the handover and give the next beginning some space.

reversed.general: Something may feel almost complete while an unfinished detail or unacknowledged lesson still asks for attention.
reversed.connection: Seek clarity about an unresolved issue rather than demanding a perfect sense of closure.
reversed.work: A final review may reveal the small task needed before you can honestly call the work finished.
reversed.advice: Define what completion actually requires and deal with that specific remainder.

upright.general: Emotional maturity means acknowledging a feeling while still choosing a measured response.
upright.connection: Offer steady care without taking over the other person's emotional life.
upright.work: Calm leadership can make a tense discussion more constructive without avoiding its substance.
upright.advice: Name the feeling, then choose the response that best serves your values.

reversed.general: Managing appearances may be replacing an honest understanding of what you feel and need.
reversed.connection: Watch for emotional pressure or withdrawal without assuming you know the motive behind it.
reversed.work: A calm exterior does not remove the need to address stress or an unfair expectation.
reversed.advice: Communicate one need directly rather than asking others to infer it.

upright.general: Sensitive attention can help you respond with empathy while keeping your own perspective intact.
upright.connection: Listen with care and leave room for the other person to describe their own experience.
upright.work: Understanding how a situation affects people can improve the way you approach the task.
upright.advice: Make space for a feeling without accepting it as the whole account of the situation.

reversed.general: Absorbing everyone's feelings can make it difficult to distinguish compassion from emotional overload.
reversed.connection: Caring does not require anticipating and solving every discomfort another person has.
reversed.work: Protect enough attention for your responsibilities instead of becoming everyone's unspoken support system.
reversed.advice: Check your own capacity before agreeing to provide more emotional care.

upright.general: An imaginative, heartfelt approach can give an idea or invitation a more human sense of purpose.
upright.connection: Express interest sincerely while leaving the other person free to respond at their own pace.
upright.work: Connect a creative proposal with the actual needs of the people it is meant to serve.
upright.advice: Turn a meaningful intention into one considerate action you can follow through on.

reversed.general: An attractive feeling or story may be running ahead of consistent action and realistic expectations.
reversed.connection: Look beyond romantic language to the reliability and respect present in the connection.
reversed.work: A beautiful proposal still needs a workable scope and dependable follow-through.
reversed.advice: Check whether the action matches the intention before investing further effort.

upright.general: A small emotional or creative discovery deserves curiosity before you decide whether it must become something larger.
upright.connection: A gentle message or honest admission can open a conversation without demanding a particular response.
upright.work: Explore an unfamiliar idea with a modest experiment rather than a large promise.
upright.advice: Give one new feeling or idea a safe, concrete form of expression.

reversed.general: Embarrassment, sensitivity or imagined rejection may be preventing a feeling from being expressed clearly.
reversed.connection: An indirect hint can be misunderstood more easily than a kind, simple statement.
reversed.work: An early creative effort does not need to be impressive before it can teach you something.
reversed.advice: Allow an imperfect first expression and stay open to a real response.

upright.general: Shared wellbeing grows through ordinary acts of belonging rather than a permanently perfect atmosphere.
upright.connection: Notice the routines and mutual consideration that help people feel at home with each other.
upright.work: Consider whether success leaves enough room for the relationships and life you value.
upright.advice: Support one shared practice that makes belonging tangible.

reversed.general: An ideal picture of happiness may be concealing different needs or making ordinary difficulties feel like failure.
reversed.connection: A connection does not have to look harmonious all the time to deserve honest care.
reversed.work: Revisit a definition of success that asks your personal life to absorb every cost.
reversed.advice: Discuss a real need instead of defending how the situation is supposed to look.

upright.general: Satisfaction becomes easier to recognise when you let an achievement be enough for a moment.
upright.connection: Enjoy what a connection offers without making another person responsible for your entire happiness.
upright.work: Acknowledge a result you worked for before immediately moving the standard further away.
upright.advice: Name something genuinely satisfying and let yourself appreciate it without comparison.

reversed.general: Getting what you wanted may reveal that the goal did not address the need underneath it.
reversed.connection: Attention and approval cannot replace a connection that fits your actual emotional needs.
reversed.work: An impressive result may still need to be weighed against the way it affects your everyday life.
reversed.advice: Ask what would feel meaningful rather than simply look desirable.

upright.general: Leaving a familiar pattern can be an act of honesty when it no longer fits what matters to you.
upright.connection: Consider whether the connection can change before assuming that endurance is the only form of loyalty.
upright.work: A once-useful goal may deserve review if pursuing it no longer has a meaningful purpose.
upright.advice: Clarify what you are moving toward, not only what you want to leave.

reversed.general: Uncertainty about staying or leaving may call for clearer criteria rather than another cycle of departure and return.
reversed.connection: Identify what would actually need to change for staying to be a willing choice.
reversed.work: Avoid abandoning a workable path solely to escape a difficulty that can be addressed.
reversed.advice: Set a review point and define what you need to learn before deciding.

upright.general: Many appealing possibilities can make it harder to distinguish a worthwhile option from an attractive imagined outcome.
upright.connection: Notice whether you are relating to the actual person or to a story about their potential.
upright.work: Compare options using real requirements and resources, not only how exciting they sound.
upright.advice: Choose one option to investigate and write down what evidence would support it.

reversed.general: A clearer view of your priorities can narrow the possibilities, though clarity still needs a practical test.
reversed.connection: Replacing an idealised picture with a direct conversation can make the connection easier to understand.
reversed.work: A shortlist is useful when it leads to a specific next step rather than another round of comparing.
reversed.advice: Choose a realistic criterion and let it remove one distracting option.

upright.general: A familiar memory or simple kindness can remind you of a value worth carrying into the present.
upright.connection: Appreciate shared history without assuming that people must remain who they used to be.
upright.work: An earlier skill or supportive connection may become useful in a new context.
upright.advice: Bring forward a helpful lesson from the past while responding to today's circumstances.

reversed.general: An idealised past can make the present look unfairly disappointing or keep an outdated role in place.
reversed.connection: Allow a person to show you who they are now rather than expecting an old connection to repeat.
reversed.work: Past success is useful experience, not proof that the same method still fits.
reversed.advice: Keep the lesson and reconsider the expectation attached to it.

upright.general: Disappointment deserves acknowledgement without becoming the only part of the situation you can see.
upright.connection: Make room for hurt while noticing which forms of care and support are still present.
upright.work: A setback may need a careful review, not a conclusion that every effort was wasted.
upright.advice: Name what was lost and one resource that remains available.

reversed.general: Recovery may begin when regret makes a little room for attention to return to the present.
reversed.connection: You can allow a new conversation without pretending that a previous hurt did not matter.
reversed.work: Reusing a lesson from a setback can help you rebuild confidence in a smaller task.
reversed.advice: Take one step toward what remains possible instead of requiring yourself to feel fully ready.

upright.general: Emotional flatness or dissatisfaction can be a cue to examine what you need before accepting more of the same.
upright.connection: Let the other person know if you need space rather than leaving silence to explain itself.
upright.work: A lack of interest may point to overload, unclear purpose or a genuine mismatch worth examining.
upright.advice: Pause to identify the need, then take a fresh look at the options already present.

reversed.general: Renewed interest can open a small route out of disengagement without requiring a dramatic new beginning.
reversed.connection: Notice an invitation to connect while keeping the freedom to respond honestly.
reversed.work: A manageable task or different perspective may help you test whether motivation can return.
reversed.advice: Try one available opening before deciding that nothing can change.

upright.general: Shared enjoyment and mutual encouragement can make an effort feel less solitary.
upright.connection: Friendship and community can support a close relationship without competing with it.
upright.work: Acknowledge collaborators and make room for an exchange of useful encouragement.
upright.advice: Include someone whose company or contribution you genuinely appreciate.

reversed.general: Group expectations can become tiring when belonging requires more participation or agreement than you can honestly give.
reversed.connection: Consider whether outside opinions are interfering with direct communication between the people involved.
reversed.work: A friendly atmosphere still needs clear responsibilities and room for constructive disagreement.
reversed.advice: Choose a social boundary that lets you participate without losing your own judgement.

upright.general: A useful exchange begins when both sides are willing to see, hear and respond to each other.
upright.connection: Look for reciprocity in attention, care and the freedom to express a different need.
upright.work: A partnership can develop through a clear agreement about what each person contributes.
upright.advice: Offer honest attention and notice whether it is returned respectfully.

reversed.general: An uneven exchange may need an honest discussion before good intentions can become a workable agreement.
reversed.connection: Different expectations do not have to be guessed; make space to name them.
reversed.work: Check whether a collaboration shares both responsibility and recognition fairly.
reversed.advice: Clarify one mismatch and see whether both sides are willing to respond.

upright.general: An opening for feeling, creativity or care can be welcomed without needing to know its final shape.
upright.connection: Allow affection to be expressed honestly while letting the connection develop at a mutual pace.
upright.work: A project that feels personally meaningful may offer a useful source of creative energy.
upright.advice: Give a new feeling a considerate, practical expression.

reversed.general: An emotional beginning may need time and self-care when you feel closed off or stretched too thin.
reversed.connection: Protect your capacity without assuming that distance is the only way to avoid hurt.
reversed.work: Creative energy may return more easily after you address strain than after you demand more inspiration.
reversed.advice: Make room to notice what you feel before asking yourself to give more.

upright.general: Clear reasoning becomes more useful when it includes responsibility for how a decision affects people.
upright.connection: Speak plainly while leaving room for feelings that cannot be resolved by argument alone.
upright.work: Use evidence and explicit criteria to make a decision others can understand.
upright.advice: Explain your reasoning and check whether the same standard is being applied fairly.

reversed.general: Certainty can become controlling when an argument leaves no room for correction or a different experience.
reversed.connection: Being articulate does not give either person the right to define the other's feelings.
reversed.work: Question a conclusion that depends more on authority than on evidence.
reversed.advice: Ask what information could change the judgement and make room to hear it.

upright.general: Discernment can protect your time and attention without requiring you to become distant or unkind.
upright.connection: A clear boundary is easier to respect when it is expressed directly rather than through a test.
upright.work: State the requirement and remove an ambiguity that keeps creating unnecessary work.
upright.advice: Say what is and is not workable while remaining open to a respectful response.

reversed.general: A protective judgement may have become sharper or more absolute than the present situation requires.
reversed.connection: Acknowledge the hurt behind a harsh response without making that response the other person's responsibility.
reversed.work: Direct feedback is most useful when it identifies a change rather than attacking a person's worth.
reversed.advice: Keep the boundary but choose words that leave a constructive way forward.

upright.general: A clear objective can mobilise energy quickly, provided speed does not replace attention to consequences.
upright.connection: A direct conversation can help if you leave enough room for an answer.
upright.work: Use your momentum on a defined task instead of rushing several unfinished arguments forward.
upright.advice: Check the aim, then act with enough attention to notice when the situation changes.

reversed.general: Urgency may be making a reaction feel necessary before its assumptions have been checked.
reversed.connection: A rapid reply can escalate a disagreement that needs a calmer question.
reversed.work: Rushed decisions and constant interruption may be costing more time than they save.
reversed.advice: Slow the next response enough to verify what problem you are actually solving.

upright.general: Curiosity becomes a strength when you ask clear questions and remain willing to revise an early conclusion.
upright.connection: Ask what you need to know without turning interest into surveillance or an interrogation.
upright.work: Investigate a new idea and record which parts are established facts and which are guesses.
upright.advice: Form one useful question and look for a reliable way to answer it.

reversed.general: An abundance of information can still produce confusion when context and verification are missing.
reversed.connection: Avoid treating a fragment of conversation or online activity as proof of someone's intention.
reversed.work: Check a claim at its source before passing it into a plan or discussion.
reversed.advice: Pause the speculation and verify one relevant detail.

upright.general: A painful limit can be acknowledged without making it a statement about the rest of your life.
upright.connection: Recognise when a familiar argument has reached its limit and needs a different response.
upright.work: A failed approach may need closure rather than more effort spent proving it should have worked.
upright.advice: Protect your immediate needs and choose a manageable next step after the ending.

reversed.general: Recovery can begin before you feel completely free of the story of what went wrong.
reversed.connection: Let a difficult experience inform your boundaries without deciding that all connections must repeat it.
reversed.work: Rebuild confidence through a limited task with a clear, achievable finish.
reversed.advice: Notice one sign of movement and allow the recovery to remain gradual.

upright.general: A worried mind may be repeating possibilities more vividly than the available evidence supports.
upright.connection: A fear about the connection is a feeling to discuss carefully, not proof about the other person.
upright.work: Write down the actual problem so it can be separated from the worst version you imagine.
upright.advice: Seek grounded support and take persistent distress seriously rather than using a card to assess it.

reversed.general: Speaking about a worry can make it more workable, even when the situation is not fully resolved.
reversed.connection: Let a trusted person hear the concern without asking them to guarantee the future.
reversed.work: A concrete conversation about expectations may reduce more strain than another private rehearsal of failure.
reversed.advice: Turn one recurring worry into a question or request that someone can respond to.

upright.general: A restricted situation calls for distinguishing real barriers from assumptions about what you are allowed to try.
upright.connection: Your ability to choose matters; seek appropriate support if a connection feels controlling or unsafe.
upright.work: Identify which constraint is fixed and which might change through information, assistance or negotiation.
upright.advice: Look for one safe option without blaming yourself for limits you did not create.

reversed.general: An additional option may become visible as you question a limiting assumption or receive practical help.
reversed.connection: A clearer boundary can restore some choice without requiring you to resolve everything alone.
reversed.work: Test a new approach on a small scale instead of assuming the old constraint applies everywhere.
reversed.advice: Take one supported step and use the result to reassess what is possible.

upright.general: Discretion and strategy can be useful, but avoiding a conversation may create a cost that grows later.
upright.connection: Distinguish a reasonable need for privacy from an agreement that requires more honest communication.
upright.work: A shortcut deserves review if it transfers hidden risks or work to someone else.
upright.advice: Choose an approach you could explain responsibly if asked about it.

reversed.general: A hidden concern or avoided responsibility may be easier to address through a direct and proportionate conversation.
reversed.connection: Focus on verified behaviour rather than treating this card as evidence of dishonesty.
reversed.work: Correct a misleading impression early instead of adding another workaround to maintain it.
reversed.advice: Clarify what happened and decide what information should be shared responsibly.

upright.general: A quieter transition can be worthwhile even when some uncertainty or sadness travels with you.
upright.connection: A change in the way you communicate may matter more than winning the old argument.
upright.work: Move toward a more workable arrangement in stages rather than requiring an instant fresh start.
upright.advice: Identify a practical support that would make the transition gentler.

reversed.general: A transition may be stalled by an unresolved issue, a missing resource or the understandable pull of familiarity.
reversed.connection: Changing the setting will not automatically change a pattern that has not been discussed.
reversed.work: Review the handover or support needed before deciding the move itself was a mistake.
reversed.advice: Name what still needs attention and address that part of the journey.

upright.general: A conflict deserves a wider view when being right risks becoming more important than the cost of the exchange.
upright.connection: An argument can have a clear winner and still leave the connection less safe or understood.
upright.work: Consider what a competitive response would do to trust and future cooperation.
upright.advice: Choose the issue worth addressing and the point at which stepping back protects your values.

reversed.general: The end of an argument can open room for repair, though agreement cannot be forced or assumed.
reversed.connection: An apology is more useful when it names a behaviour and leaves space for the other person's response.
reversed.work: Acknowledge the cost of the conflict and define how the next disagreement should be handled.
reversed.advice: Offer one responsible repair without demanding immediate reconciliation.

upright.general: Rest can be an active part of responding well rather than a reward you must earn by becoming exhausted.
upright.connection: Explain a need for quiet time so that a pause is not mistaken for punishment.
upright.work: A deliberate break may help you return with a clearer view of an overloaded task.
upright.advice: Give the pause a useful boundary and let yourself disengage from one demand.

reversed.general: Restlessness or an overdue return can make it difficult to find the right balance between recovery and movement.
reversed.connection: Check whether time apart is restoring you or postponing a necessary conversation.
reversed.work: Return gradually if you are ready, or adjust the load if recovery has not been possible.
reversed.advice: Choose a sustainable pace instead of switching between total withdrawal and overwork.

upright.general: A painful feeling becomes easier to approach when it can be acknowledged without being treated as a permanent identity.
upright.connection: Speak about a hurt using what you experienced rather than assumptions about another person's motives.
upright.work: Difficult feedback or disappointment may need time before it becomes a useful next action.
upright.advice: Allow a truthful expression of the feeling and seek care rather than forcing an instant solution.

reversed.general: Healing may involve revisiting a hurt differently, not proving that it no longer matters.
reversed.connection: Forgiveness, repair and renewed closeness are separate choices; none has to be rushed.
reversed.work: Separate an old disappointment from the facts of the opportunity in front of you.
reversed.advice: Notice what would help you carry the experience with less self-blame.

upright.general: A difficult choice may need a missing fact or a clearer priority before further comparison becomes useful.
upright.connection: Keeping the peace indefinitely can leave both people unsure of what you actually need.
upright.work: Identify the decision criterion instead of giving every possible outcome equal weight.
upright.advice: Ask what information or value would genuinely help you decide.

reversed.general: Avoided choices can become more manageable once the conflict is named, even if the answer remains imperfect.
reversed.connection: A simple statement of uncertainty can be more honest than silent agreement.
reversed.work: Reduce the number of competing inputs and decide who owns the next decision.
reversed.advice: Choose a manageable decision point rather than waiting for every doubt to vanish.

upright.general: A precise question or honest insight can cut through confusion and make the next action easier to define.
upright.connection: Clarity grows through direct words that are both truthful and considerate.
upright.work: Define the problem in a sentence that another person could test or respond to.
upright.advice: Check the insight against evidence and use it to clarify one next step.

reversed.general: A promising idea may still be clouded by imprecise language, incomplete evidence or a conclusion reached too quickly.
reversed.connection: Check what was meant before reacting to the strongest interpretation of a statement.
reversed.work: An unclear requirement needs clarification before it becomes a confident estimate or commitment.
reversed.advice: Rewrite the question plainly and verify the assumption underneath it.

upright.general: A clear sense of purpose can help you lead an effort without needing to control every detail of it.
upright.connection: Share what you hope to build while making room for the other person's independent aims.
upright.work: Set a direction others can understand and support the people who turn it into real work.
upright.advice: Turn a broad ambition into a clear invitation and a realistic next milestone.

reversed.general: A strong vision can become demanding when impatience or pride leaves no room for feedback.
reversed.connection: Check whether your enthusiasm has become an expectation that others must follow your pace.
reversed.work: Leadership needs realistic resources and listening, not just the ability to announce a bold target.
reversed.advice: Ask for one honest objection and use it to improve the plan.

upright.general: Warm confidence can make it easier to participate fully without needing to be the most impressive person present.
upright.connection: Let your interests and personality be visible while welcoming the other person's distinctiveness.
upright.work: Bring your initiative to a task where your enthusiasm can encourage rather than overshadow others.
upright.advice: Show up as yourself and make one confident contribution.

reversed.general: Comparison or pressure to appear confident may be drawing attention away from your actual interests and energy.
reversed.connection: A need for reassurance can be expressed directly without competing for attention.
reversed.work: Your contribution does not have to resemble someone else's style to be valuable.
reversed.advice: Return to one activity you enjoy without measuring how it looks to others.

upright.general: Energy and a willingness to explore can help an idea move beyond an exciting conversation.
upright.connection: Welcome shared adventure while being clear about what you can realistically commit to.
upright.work: Use your momentum to test a promising direction with a defined beginning and end.
upright.advice: Give your enthusiasm a useful task and a point at which to review the result.

reversed.general: Restless movement can turn a series of exciting starts into unfinished obligations.
reversed.connection: Intensity needs dependable follow-through if another person is being asked to rely on it.
reversed.work: Check which existing commitment would carry the cost of starting something new.
reversed.advice: Finish or consciously close one task before chasing the next burst of energy.

upright.general: A new interest deserves an experiment that lets curiosity become experience rather than only a future possibility.
upright.connection: A shared activity can reveal more than trying to plan the whole connection in advance.
upright.work: Explore a skill or idea through a small piece of work you can actually attempt.
upright.advice: Make the first experiment small enough that learning matters more than looking accomplished.

reversed.general: Uncertainty about where to begin can scatter a good idea across too many imagined directions.
reversed.connection: An exciting possibility still needs a clear and considerate invitation.
reversed.work: A first attempt that feels awkward is useful information, not proof that the idea is worthless.
reversed.advice: Choose one simple starting point and let the result guide the next adjustment.

upright.general: Responsibility becomes harder to carry when every task is treated as equally urgent or yours alone.
upright.connection: Discuss the actual division of effort rather than measuring love by how much you can endure.
upright.work: A heavy workload needs priorities, realistic scope and visible ownership of each obligation.
upright.advice: Identify one task to delegate, defer or renegotiate.

reversed.general: Putting down a burden can restore capacity, provided you make a deliberate choice about what still needs care.
reversed.connection: You can ask for a fairer arrangement without proving that you are unable to manage anything.
reversed.work: Clarify which responsibilities must be completed and which were accumulated without a real agreement.
reversed.advice: Reduce the load openly instead of quietly dropping work that others still depend on.

upright.general: Experience can support persistence when you protect enough energy to continue thoughtfully.
upright.connection: A boundary can honour past experience without assuming that every new interaction is the same threat.
upright.work: Use what previous difficulties taught you to make the next attempt more sustainable.
upright.advice: Protect one essential limit and ask what support would make continued effort reasonable.

reversed.general: Constant vigilance may be costing more energy than the situation currently requires.
reversed.connection: Check whether a protective habit is still helping or is preventing a respectful connection from developing.
reversed.work: Persistence is not always the best response when fatigue is reducing judgement and available capacity.
reversed.advice: Reassess the demand before deciding that you simply need to push harder.

upright.general: Momentum can carry several things forward quickly when communication and direction are already clear.
upright.connection: Respond to an active conversation with attention rather than assuming speed means deeper understanding.
upright.work: Coordinate the next steps so that fast progress does not create avoidable confusion.
upright.advice: Confirm the message, the recipient and the next action before moving quickly.

reversed.general: Delay or crossed messages may be asking for coordination rather than another attempt to increase urgency.
reversed.connection: A late reply can have many explanations; clarify expectations instead of inventing a motive.
reversed.work: Check a dependency or unclear handover before adding pressure to the timeline.
reversed.advice: Slow down long enough to identify where the message or task is getting stuck.

upright.general: Standing by a considered position can be useful without requiring you to defend every preference as a battle.
upright.connection: Express a limit in terms of your needs rather than an attempt to control the response.
upright.work: Protect a justified priority while remaining open to evidence that could improve your position.
upright.advice: Decide which principle matters enough to defend and explain it plainly.

reversed.general: Defending too many positions at once can make it difficult to recognise which disagreements actually matter.
reversed.connection: A conversation may become easier when you stop treating every difference as a challenge to your worth.
reversed.work: Review whether a protected approach still serves the goal or mainly preserves past effort.
reversed.advice: Conserve energy by choosing a necessary boundary and releasing a less important contest.

upright.general: Recognition can affirm useful effort when it also leaves room to appreciate the support behind the result.
upright.connection: Celebrate each other's progress without making affection depend on achievement or public approval.
upright.work: Share a concrete success and acknowledge the collaborators who helped it happen.
upright.advice: Accept appreciation and identify the practice you want to continue.

reversed.general: A need for visible approval can hide progress that is meaningful but not widely noticed.
reversed.connection: The quality of a connection is not established by how convincingly it is displayed to others.
reversed.work: Clarify the difference between useful feedback and the recognition you hoped would settle self-doubt.
reversed.advice: Use an honest measure of progress that does not depend entirely on applause.

upright.general: Different aims can create friction that becomes useful only when people agree how to work through it.
upright.connection: A disagreement can reveal needs without becoming a contest over who is more entitled to have them.
upright.work: Clarify roles and decision criteria so that competing ideas can be compared constructively.
upright.advice: Find the shared problem underneath the competing positions.

reversed.general: Avoided disagreement can keep tension in place even when everyone appears to be cooperating.
reversed.connection: Polite silence may need a safe opportunity for each person to describe what is not working.
reversed.work: Surface a practical conflict before unclear priorities turn it into personal resentment.
reversed.advice: Address one specific difference without asking everyone to settle every disagreement at once.

upright.general: A reliable base and a shared milestone can make room for celebration without requiring the whole journey to be complete.
upright.connection: Shared routines and welcoming spaces can make commitment visible in everyday life.
upright.work: Mark a completed stage and make sure the support around it is ready for the next one.
upright.advice: Celebrate a real milestone and acknowledge the foundation that supports it.

reversed.general: An unsettled foundation can make a celebration feel premature or leave someone outside the sense of belonging.
reversed.connection: Discuss what helps each person feel welcome instead of assuming a shared idea of home or commitment.
reversed.work: Check whether a completed milestone has the practical support needed to remain reliable.
reversed.advice: Repair one part of the foundation before putting more expectations on it.

upright.general: A wider view can help you prepare for growth after the first step has already been taken.
upright.connection: Talk about the direction you each imagine rather than assuming that present closeness implies the same plans.
upright.work: Consider the resources, partners and time that would make a next stage realistic.
upright.advice: Look beyond the immediate task and prepare one useful connection or dependency.

reversed.general: An expansion may need adjustment when expectations have moved further ahead than the current foundation can support.
reversed.connection: A future plan may need smaller agreements that both people can genuinely commit to now.
reversed.work: Review the assumption behind a delay before treating it as a reason to abandon the whole direction.
reversed.advice: Strengthen the next stage you can reach instead of extending the plan indefinitely.

upright.general: Choosing a direction can turn a broad wish into a plan while still leaving room to learn along the way.
upright.connection: Share your own aims clearly enough that a joint plan can be a choice rather than an assumption.
upright.work: Compare a familiar option with a new direction using your actual priorities and available resources.
upright.advice: Choose a small planning step that would make one option easier to evaluate.

reversed.general: Fear of an imperfect choice can keep planning active long after it stops producing useful information.
reversed.connection: Ask whether uncertainty is being communicated or left for the other person to interpret.
reversed.work: An additional plan will not resolve a decision that needs a clear priority or a modest experiment.
reversed.advice: Set a realistic decision point and identify what you can test safely before it.

upright.general: A spark of interest can become a worthwhile beginning when you give it attention and a practical outlet.
upright.connection: Enjoy attraction or shared enthusiasm without treating a strong beginning as a promise of lasting compatibility.
upright.work: A fresh idea deserves a small prototype that tests whether the energy can become useful work.
upright.advice: Act on the spark in one limited way before it becomes another untested possibility.

reversed.general: A delayed start may reflect depleted energy, an unclear aim or a beginning that is not ready to be forced.
reversed.connection: A connection can develop at different speeds; clarity and consent matter more than manufactured intensity.
reversed.work: Check whether the missing ingredient is time, purpose or a more manageable first task.
reversed.advice: Make room for the idea without demanding that inspiration immediately become commitment.

upright.general: Dependability grows through careful stewardship of the resources and responsibilities already in your hands.
upright.connection: Practical support matters most when it respects the other person's independence and priorities.
upright.work: Sustainable success asks for clear commitments, realistic maintenance and a responsible view of available resources.
upright.advice: Strengthen one dependable practice instead of relying on an impressive one-time gesture.

reversed.general: Security can become restrictive when status, possessions or control are treated as the only measures of worth.
reversed.connection: Providing something useful does not entitle either person to direct the other's choices.
reversed.work: Review whether protecting an established position is preventing a necessary practical adjustment.
reversed.advice: Separate genuine stability from the need to appear successful or remain in control.

upright.general: Practical care can make daily life more supportive through small arrangements that are useful and sustainable.
upright.connection: Consider the ordinary acts that help both people feel supported without assigning care to one person alone.
upright.work: Organise your time and resources in a way that supports both the task and the person doing it.
upright.advice: Make one everyday need easier to meet with a realistic routine.

reversed.general: Looking after everything else can leave too little capacity for the ordinary care you also need.
reversed.connection: A dependable role should not prevent you from asking to receive support in return.
reversed.work: Check whether practical responsibilities have grown without a corresponding change in time or help.
reversed.advice: Include your own needs in the plan instead of treating them as what happens after everything else.

upright.general: Consistent, unglamorous effort can produce a reliable foundation when each step serves a clear purpose.
upright.connection: Dependable behaviour can express commitment more clearly than occasional dramatic reassurance.
upright.work: A repeatable process and careful follow-through may be more useful than seeking a faster-looking route.
upright.advice: Complete the next practical step and make it easy to repeat responsibly.

reversed.general: A dependable routine can become an obstacle when repetition replaces a review of whether it still works.
reversed.connection: Reliability does not have to exclude curiosity, shared enjoyment or a needed change in habit.
reversed.work: Look for a process maintained by familiarity rather than a clear benefit to the task.
reversed.advice: Keep the useful discipline and test one small improvement to the routine.

upright.general: A practical skill develops when curiosity is supported by focused study and a chance to apply what you learn.
upright.connection: Show interest through attention to a real need rather than a promise you have not thought through.
upright.work: Choose a useful skill and practise it on a limited task with clear feedback.
upright.advice: Turn the intention to improve into one concrete learning exercise.

reversed.general: An intention may remain theoretical when preparation, distraction or fear of being a beginner replaces practice.
reversed.connection: A helpful intention needs a specific action that the other person actually welcomes.
reversed.work: More materials or plans may not solve a problem that needs a small attempt and feedback.
reversed.advice: Reduce the task until you can practise it today and review what you learned.

upright.general: Long-term support is built from the structures, shared knowledge and dependable resources that outlast a single achievement.
upright.connection: Discuss the practical values you hope to share rather than assuming a common view of security or family.
upright.work: Consider how today's work can remain useful, understandable and maintainable for the people who inherit it.
upright.advice: Care for a shared foundation and make its responsibilities explicit.

reversed.general: An inherited definition of success may carry obligations that no longer fit the life you want to build.
reversed.connection: Family expectations and material comfort do not automatically determine what makes a connection right for you.
reversed.work: Review the actual sustainability of an arrangement instead of relying on its established appearance.
reversed.advice: Identify what you value in the tradition and which expectation needs to be reconsidered.

upright.general: Personal independence can be appreciated as the result of skills, boundaries and support developed over time.
upright.connection: A close connection can add to a life you value without requiring either person to give up their individuality.
upright.work: Recognise a capability that now gives you more choice in how you use your time and effort.
upright.advice: Enjoy a concrete benefit of your work while protecting the habits that sustain it.

reversed.general: Appearing independent or accomplished can become costly when it prevents an honest view of your needs and resources.
reversed.connection: Receiving help does not make your own contribution or independence less real.
reversed.work: Compare the actual value of an achievement with the effort spent maintaining its appearance.
reversed.advice: Choose a measure of wellbeing that is meaningful even when no one else sees it.

upright.general: Craft improves through repeated attention to a specific detail and a willingness to learn from feedback.
upright.connection: A connection can benefit from practising a small communication skill rather than waiting for effort to feel effortless.
upright.work: Focus on the part of the craft that makes the result more dependable, not merely more polished.
upright.advice: Practise one skill with a clear standard and review the result honestly.

reversed.general: Repetition loses value when perfectionism or disengagement prevents you from noticing whether the effort is useful.
reversed.connection: More effort is not always better if it repeats a response the other person has said is unhelpful.
reversed.work: Check whether further polishing addresses a real requirement or delays finishing an adequate result.
reversed.advice: Define what good enough means for this task before doing another round of work.

upright.general: A considered review can distinguish slow development from effort that needs a different direction.
upright.connection: Look at how the connection is developing over time rather than demanding a milestone to settle uncertainty.
upright.work: Compare progress, remaining cost and purpose before deciding whether continued effort is worthwhile.
upright.advice: Set a realistic review point and use evidence rather than impatience to assess progress.

reversed.general: Past effort does not by itself prove that continuing in the same way is the most useful choice.
reversed.connection: Time already invested cannot replace a present willingness to communicate and care for each other.
reversed.work: Review a stalled commitment without treating its previous cost as a reason it must continue unchanged.
reversed.advice: Decide what would justify the next stage of effort instead of defending the last one.

upright.general: A healthy exchange considers capacity, need and choice instead of expecting every contribution to look identical.
upright.connection: Offer and receive support in ways that preserve dignity and room to say no.
upright.work: Clarify the terms of assistance, recognition or shared resources so that expectations are understood.
upright.advice: Ask what a fair exchange would look like for the people actually involved.

reversed.general: An uneven exchange can become uncomfortable when help carries unspoken conditions or one person's limits are ignored.
reversed.connection: Support should not be used to create guilt, obligation or control over another person's choices.
reversed.work: Check whether responsibility and recognition are being distributed as clearly as the benefits.
reversed.advice: Make the conditions explicit before offering or accepting more than feels workable.

upright.general: A sense of scarcity or exclusion calls for practical support, not a judgement about your value or future.
upright.connection: Share a need with someone trustworthy rather than assuming you must hide every difficulty to be accepted.
upright.work: Identify the immediate resource gap and look for reliable information or appropriate assistance.
upright.advice: Choose one concrete source of support; a card cannot determine your actual financial security.

reversed.general: A gradual improvement may begin through accepting help, finding a resource or making a difficulty easier to name.
reversed.connection: Let a supportive response challenge the belief that you have to manage everything alone.
reversed.work: A small practical improvement can be useful without proving that every concern is now resolved.
reversed.advice: Build on the support available and give the recovery a realistic pace.

upright.general: Protecting what you have can support security, though excessive control may leave too little room to adapt.
upright.connection: A wish for reassurance does not make it reasonable to restrict the other person's freedom.
upright.work: Review whether a reserve, routine or boundary is serving a clear practical purpose.
upright.advice: Name what you need to protect and where a little flexibility is safe.

reversed.general: Loosening a restrictive grip can create room for change, provided release remains deliberate rather than impulsive.
reversed.connection: Giving someone space can coexist with clear agreements about what you both need.
reversed.work: Reconsider a rule that protects resources at the expense of a genuinely useful improvement.
reversed.advice: Make one measured adjustment instead of responding to restriction by abandoning every limit.

upright.general: Useful collaboration grows when different skills are respected and a shared standard makes the work easier to coordinate.
upright.connection: A shared task can become a chance to understand how each person prefers to contribute.
upright.work: Make roles and feedback clear so that expertise can combine rather than compete.
upright.advice: Ask for a specific contribution and show how it connects to the common goal.

reversed.general: A shared effort can stall when roles, standards or respect for different contributions remain unclear.
reversed.connection: An uneven practical arrangement needs a conversation about actual work, not a guess about willingness.
reversed.work: Clarify ownership and the definition of completion before interpreting a coordination problem as personal failure.
reversed.advice: Agree on who does what and how the result will be reviewed.

upright.general: Flexibility can help you manage changing demands when you remain aware of your actual capacity.
upright.connection: Discuss time and attention openly instead of expecting care to fit invisibly around every other obligation.
upright.work: A workable schedule needs room for adjustments rather than assuming every task will take its best-case time.
upright.advice: Choose the priority for today and leave some room for a change in circumstances.

reversed.general: Too many competing demands may need fewer commitments rather than a more elaborate way to juggle them.
reversed.connection: An overloaded schedule is worth acknowledging before repeated cancellations become an unspoken pattern.
reversed.work: Make trade-offs visible and renegotiate a commitment that no longer fits the available time.
reversed.advice: Remove, defer or share one demand instead of promising to handle everything better.

upright.general: A tangible opportunity becomes meaningful through attention, practical preparation and the effort needed to sustain it.
upright.connection: A small dependable gesture can provide a better foundation than an ambitious promise.
upright.work: Examine the real requirements of a new task or opportunity before deciding how it fits your resources.
upright.advice: Take one concrete step that lets you learn about the opportunity without overcommitting.

reversed.general: A promising opening may need more preparation or a clearer view of its costs before it becomes workable.
reversed.connection: Good intentions need realistic time and effort if another person is being asked to rely on them.
reversed.work: Check the details of an appealing opportunity rather than treating its appearance as proof of value.
reversed.advice: Clarify a practical condition before committing resources you cannot easily replace.
